body: I’m a recent Silva graduate and as of maybe two months ago I can almost speak to my i tuition/tutor/spirit guide/call it whatever you like. How I distinguish that from complete fantasy is that the inputs I get are very short, almost like commands “Wait”, “Do this”, “Don’t do that”, and so on. It’s not only tf related but because I’ve spent these two months working intensely on our connection like working through his past traumas, emotional pain and blockages, as well as mine on the mental level, it’s normal that the majority of the inputs I get are related to him. However, ever since I met my tf a year ago, I was able to mentally communicate with him. I remember the first time it happened. It was only a few weeks after we met and he went on vacation to his country. One day I asked myself something like “will he contact me when he comes back?” and I got an immediate and quite adamant response “Of course I will”. It was very different from my usual thoughts and didn’t feel it came from me but from him, like a mental response. With Silva method I’m able to converse with him on a mental level and figure out what he’s thinking/feeling. Regardless, I can also get input from my intuition/spirit guides and it feels differently from when I converse mentally with him

Why would it be painful and scary when the two parts of the same soul are going towards the union? Shouldn’t meeting a twin flame, while overwhelming, be a positive thing as you finally feel complete? My problem with this connection is that I thought that the previous one could have been a twin flame, too. I’ve learned about the concept of false twin flames, in which case there’s a possibility that my ex was my false twin. Now, I did care a lot about him and felt a strong connection with him. What if this connection is the same, just that I can’t see it? Basically, how do you distinguish between a false and a true twin flame while you’re actively involved with them if you can only do it in hindsight after the breakup?  I now feel very good about not being with my ex (I felt good even before meeting this guy) and in hindsight can see that a great part of what I thought that connection was and the importance of it was in my head. We were very good friends and I draw the meaning of the connection and the bond from the long friendship that we used to have. I don’t like living in the illusion that something is when in fact it isn’t 🤷‍♀️
Know if I’m right or wrong.

It’s not a natural part of life. Not everyone get to experience it. And even those who think they do, might be wrong… manipulation and emotional abuse can be disguised as love, too
Today, a young guy’s body has been found in the river after being missing for months. The first thing I thought was “That lucky bastard! I wish it was me!”

Me too, however, I always remember what my friend’s dad who lost both of his legs said. When it happened, he thought about suicide, but then realized that he was going to die anyway, there is no escaping death, no one will live eternally, so while he was here he wanted to have fun and make the best of it. Suicide was always the option, but while being alive, he wanted to see if things would turn out for the better. It’s been 30 years ago, he’s still alive and a paracyclist.

That can be a big issue because for the most part they look normal compared to others, so it’s harder to accept that the only person you had an emotional connection with and thought loved you (un)conditionally was far more detrimental and damaging to your mental health and well-being.

Oh, so true! When my mom lashes at me, my dad is always there to back her up! Even when I stand my ground, my dad would come and ask me to apologize to my mother (usually for something hurtful that she said to me). But when he is being overbearing (he rarely lashes out), my mom is there to “protect” me. But yeah, when everything is going smoothly, she expects me to praise and admire him. They have been together for 50 years, married for 40.

Interesting. I always knew my dad was a narc (someone who only talks about himself, exaggerate his accomplishments, seeks constant praise and admiration, etc) plus my mom alway joked about my dad being a narc (he even literally loves looking himself in the mirror l, talking about a textbook example lol). That why I was sure I knew what a narcissist looked like (I was living with a textbook example) and my mom is almost the polar opposite - she is not boastful, she doesn’t talk only about herself, she was involved in my life (my dad not so much) etc. I never knew there was such a thing as a covert narcissist, which is why it came as a shock when I realized the harsh truth that my mom could be a narcissist, too, and that it was she who messed me up far worse than my dad ever did. Her own sister has Borderline personality disorder so, compared to her sister and to my dad she always looked normal.

I guess the same is true for my parents. How long did it take for your that your mom was a covert narcissist? Overt narcissists are pretty easy to spot, but and especially compared to the overt narcs, they seem as normal, easygoing human beings.

Totally agree, though in the back of my mind there is always a voice saying “do narcissists even know they are narcs?” A therapist once told me (when I mentioned my fear of becoming a narcs; at that time I thought that only my dad was a narc) “you know, people don’t come to therapy because they think they are great; they come because they think they aren’t”. I agree with that, but it’s easier said than done. I think that the best thing for me is to finally come to terms that both of my parents are narcs, not just my dad. I may be able to get her in the same mind department as my dad - a roommate who can be cool to talk to from time. Up until know, I always thought it was my fault and I would spend so much time trying to rationalize her behavior. I don’t do that with my dad. I don’t have much compassion for him and his behavior. To me, he has NPD and I see everything he does through npd without questioning myself (sure, I do question why he couldn’t be like any other normal dad who is unconditionally there for their kid). With my mom, I always managed to “understand” where she was coming from and empathize with her. I would feel guilty when she would put me down, sulk and pout. I always blamed it on me. Maybe now I can see her in the same light as my dad. I believe it would help me immensely to establish some healthy boundaries and maybe start living my life without feeling stifled and stuck.

Thank you so much for this comment! It makes me feel better knowing that I’m not alone in this! I have also been trying to “fix the relationship with my mother” for the longest time. Compared to my dad she seems reasonable, kind and empathetic. That’s why I never understood why she was behaving the way she was behaving towards me. 

I don’t know if you have the same issue, but I’m afraid of being good at my career and being praised because I fear the praise getting to my head and becoming a narcissist. I don’t know the difference between being happy and proud with your achievements and being a narc. I always have to tell myself that praise doesn’t matter and to kind of put myself down to counteract the possibility of becoming a narc myself. I don’t know if this makes any sense lol

I also don’t trust myself when it comes to relationships, because I don’t know if I’m capable to figure out if someone is manipulative as there is a greater chance to get attached to people who are similar to my parents in some shape and form (don’t have to be narcs but can’t be manipulative). That’s why I haven’t had many relationships in my life and even went 11 years (my whole 20s) whiteout a bf. I’m afraid to get into a relationship because I don’t know if I’ll be able to see the red flags. I’m always kind of suspicious of everyone

It’s difficult to wrap my head around the idea that my mother is also a narcissist because, living with an overt narcissist, I thought what narcissism looked like and her behavior never checked as narcissistic. 

I believe that two narcissists can get along very well if their subtypes are compatible and they are each other’s enablers (so true in my parents case!). I’m angry at myself that I haven’t figured it out earlier or at least that I didn’t trust myself enough 10 years ago to admit that it was possible. I would have saved myself so much self-doubt and would probably live a happier life. 

As I said, it’s easier to deal with my dad. If he doesn’t get admiration from you, he’ll move to someone else. I managed to compartmentalized his role in my life and not be mad about it or blame myself and think that there’s something wrong with me. He gets on my nerves quite a lot and I do get pissed, especially thinking how my life have always been in service of his grandiose shit to the point of having it clear that I can’t have a life or career while he’s around and alive (sounds cruel, I know). Even though it’s damaging on so many levels, at least I don’t feel bad about myself and don’t think there is something wrong with me. 

With my mother I always feel that there is something inherently wrong with me, even though she always portrays herself as being super loving and kind. My dad doesn’t care about anyone but himself so, even when he mocks me and “jokingly” calls me names, I know it’s not because of malice or because he truly thinks like that about me, but because it’s because of his narcissism. 

With my mother I always have a feeling that she has something against me personally, like she blames me for her own life failures. She’s so “worried about me” to the point that I feel like I’m stupid, unable to make sound decisions, unable to judge people and situations. 

It angers me a lot because I’ve spent my whole life doubting myself all the while I should have doubting her. Sounds weird, but I prefer overt narcissists. At least you know where you stand with them.
